title: Composed Workflow Evaluation: LLM + Retrieval + Deterministic Validator + Emulator (Preregistration)
research_question: Does a reproducible composed evaluation workflow that integrates LLM proposals, retrieval-constrained templating, deterministic validators (Batfish/NetKAT), and an emulator (Mininet) reduce the rate of emulator-detected unsafe/executable faults compared with LLM-only generation on a paired set of natural-language NetOps intents?
confirmatory_hypotheses: H1 (primary): The composed workflow (LLM → retrieval+templating → deterministic validator → emulator/rollback) yields a lower paired unsafe-execution rate than LLM-only generation (two-sided).
H2 (secondary): The composed workflow yields a lower emulator-fault count per intent (mean counts) than LLM-only generation.
exploratory_questions: E1: How do effects vary by intent complexity strata (simple/moderate/complex)?
E2: What is the observed validator false-negative rate estimated via cross-validator checks (Batfish vs NetKAT) on a held-out coverage set?
E3: What fraction of composed-workflow blocks are false-blocks (valid proposals rejected by validator pipeline)?
benchmark_scope: Synthetic+publicly-derived Intent Corpus (n=200) synthesized from public configuration templates and ticket-style prompts; scope limited to IPv4 routing, ACLs, basic switching, and topology manipulations supported by Mininet/Batfish/NetKAT.
Held-out validator-coverage test set (n=50) used only to estimate validator false-negative rates and cross-validator disagreements; not used in confirmatory primary test.
model_scope: Single hosted LLM API provider (hosted_model_api_available=true). Exact model identifier will be fixed and recorded in execution metadata prior to runs.
All LLM calls via hosted API (CPU-backed); no local GPU execution or vendor-internal modification.
transformation_scope: Retrieval-constrained templating (local retrieval index of templates with deterministic snapshot/checksum), slot-filling into vendor-neutral templates, syntax/grammar emission to Mininet-compatible scripts.
Deterministic validation via Batfish (reachability, isolation, ACL compliance) and NetKAT cross-checks where applicable; automatic syntax regex checks and harmful-command filtering.
primary_estimand: Per-intent paired difference in unsafe-execution outcome: probability that an intent would produce an emulator-detected unsafe executable fault under LLM-only minus probability under the composed workflow (paired on the same intent).
secondary_estimands: Mean emulator-detected fault count per intent per treatment (LLM-only vs composed).
Per-intent false-block rate: proportion of composed-workflow proposals rejected by validator but which the emulator would have accepted (estimated via targeted replays on a sampled subset).
Per-intent latency and token-usage cost per treatment (for cost-effectiveness reporting).
sampling_plan: Confirmatory corpus: n=200 intents sampled deterministically from the synthetic/public template pool stratified into three complexity strata (simple: 80, moderate: 80, complex: 40). For each intent run two paired treatments: (A) LLM-only generation and (B) Composed workflow. Deterministic RNG seeds used for all sampling and audit draws. Discovery (validator-coverage) set: 50 additional stratified intents used only for validator false-negative estimation and cross-validator checks.
power_and_precision_plan: Primary estimand: paired per-intent absolute difference in unsafe-execution probability. Target effect: detect ~7.5 percentage-point absolute reduction (e.g., 15%→7.5%). Method: paired McNemar test (two-sided, alpha=0.05) for binary unsafe outcomes; report 95% Wilson CIs, absolute/relative risk reductions, and number-needed-to-protect. With n=200 pairs and assumed baseline unsafe 10–20%, approximate power ≈0.80 to detect ~6–8% absolute reductions depending on discordant counts. Secondary: compare mean fault counts via paired Wilcoxon signed-rank (or paired t-test if diagnostics permit) with bootstrap 95% CIs (10,000 replicates). Sensitivity analyses: recompute MDE for baseline unsafe rates 5/10/15/25%; bootstrap CIs and per-stratum diagnostics. All analyses use preregistered seeds and deterministic scoring scripts.
exclusion_rules: Exclude any intent whose retrieval-index snapshot checksum differs from the preregistered snapshot (contamination flag).

If an LLM/validator/emulator call fails after the preregistered retry policy (total attempts=3), mark that paired intent as a technical failure and exclude it from the primary per-protocol confirmatory analysis (see missingness_plan for ITT sensitivity analyses).

Automatically reject outputs containing tokens matching the preregistered harmful-command regex; such rejections are logged and treated according to the composed-workflow retry/block rules (may count as validator-block).
missingness_plan: Automatic retry policy for transient technical failures: up to 2 retries after the initial attempt (total attempts=3) with exponential backoff. If after retries the call still fails, classify as technical-failure for that treatment; exclude the affected paired intent from the primary per-protocol analysis and record full logs. Conduct ITT sensitivity analyses where technical-failure cases are imputed conservatively as 'unsafe' for the impacted treatment (worst-case imputations) and report both per-protocol and ITT results. All retry counts, timestamps, and raw logs retained and disclosed.
analysis_plan: Primary analysis: paired McNemar test (two-sided) on binary emulator-detected unsafe-execution outcomes per intent; report exact p-values, 95% Wilson CIs for proportions, absolute and relative risk reductions, and number-needed-to-protect. Secondary analysis: paired comparison of emulator-fault counts using Wilcoxon signed-rank (or paired t-test if normality holds) with bootstrap 95% CIs (10,000 replicates). Estimate validator false-negative rate on discovery set and via audit resampling; report confusion tables for validator vs emulator outcomes. Exploratory subgroup analyses by complexity strata labeled exploratory and corrected under the multiplicity_plan. All code for scoring, tests, and bootstrap is deterministic, seeded, and stored in the execution manifest.
multiplicity_plan: H1 is the single preregistered confirmatory test. Secondary and exploratory tests (H2, strata analyses, false-block rate) are exploratory. When reporting multiple exploratory p-values, apply Benjamini-Hochberg FDR control at q=0.10 and report unadjusted p-values alongside adjusted thresholds. Explicitly label exploratory findings and avoid strong confirmatory language for them.
contamination_plan: Risk factors: (1) retrieval-index contamination (inadvertent inclusion of environment-specific or harmful commands), (2) validator-emulator semantic mismatch (Batfish/NetKAT not covering all semantic intent modes), (3) API outages or rate-limiting causing missing paired data. Detection: deterministic checksum/versioning for retrieval snapshot; automated cross-validator consistency checks on discovery set (Batfish vs NetKAT) and disagreement logging; runtime logging of API error codes and deterministic flagging of outages/rate-limits. Item-flagging rules: any intent/template whose retrieval snapshot checksum differs from preregistered snapshot is flagged and excluded from confirmatory analysis; any composed output with harmful-command regex match is rejected and recorded (no execution). Analysis treatment: primary analysis excludes flagged/contaminated items and reports a contamination audit table; sensitivity analyses re-run with flagged items included and explicitly labeled. Residual uncertainty documented for retrieval omissions and validator blindspots.
stopping_rule: Stop conditions before claiming confirmatory results: (1) If >20% of confirmatory paired intents are excluded due to technical failures or contamination, pause execution and report inability to support primary confirmatory test (abort confirmatory claims; continue to publish execution logs and sensitivity analyses). (2) If a provider outage or systematic rate-limiting prevents completion of preregistered planned_model_calls within the wall-clock allowance despite retries, stop and report incomplete execution with full logs. Per-intent generation stops after max retries (3 attempts); if still invalid, record as 'validator-block' and proceed per exclusion rules.
planned_outputs: Deterministic retrieval-index snapshot and checksum manifest.
All experiment code and configuration (scoring, seeding, deterministic orchestration scripts).
Raw model-call logs, validator outputs, emulator traces, and hashes for all artifacts.
Execution manifest recording retries, errors, and timestamps.
Statistical results file with primary and secondary test outputs and bootstrap CIs.
Evidence-to-claim table and nearest-work comparison matrix.
Complete IEEE LaTeX manuscript (≤5 pages) including mandatory Disclosure Statement.
Autonomous revision log and final-output hash manifest.
